authority_posture: navigation record of checked, tracked corpus boundaries; not a claim registry, proof authority, or a statement of problem status
scope: Existing-corpus route memory for the eight-problem public portfolio. First verify the record shape with `python3 scripts/query_route_memory.py --validate`, then select a record with `python3 scripts/query_route_memory.py --problem <number>` (or `--all`) and follow its evidence path and named anchors into checked Lean. Each entry records only the located route and its stated boundary.
recording_rule: A negative result is local to the route and assumptions named below. An inconclusive record is not an impossibility result.

records.actual_established: The conditional no-repeat criterion implies irrationality, and two consecutive threshold failures on the distinguished orbit have an exact two-cylinder classification.
records.failure_boundary: The evidence does not establish the no-consecutive-failures hypothesis for the factorial-gap orbit and does not say that either cylinder occurs cofinally.
records.prerequisites_and_assumptions: The implication assumes eventual exclusion of consecutive predecessor-gap threshold failures on the distinguished factorial-gap orbit.
records.next_obligation: Establish that orbit-level no-repeat hypothesis, or replace this conditional route with a separately evidenced one.

records.route: Clean-recovery length as a normalized-mass descent certificate
records.actual_established: A checked nine-step primitive clean recovery returns normalized negative mass from 1/11 to 1/11 while its initial payment is four, below both its length and 2^9.
records.failure_boundary: This rules out a strict descent or payment lower bound determined only by the displayed normalized coordinate and clean-recovery length; it does not classify all primitive-tail invariants.
records.prerequisites_and_assumptions: The route uses the centered primitive cocycle and the exact clean-recovery witness encoded in the cited module.
records.next_obligation: Any replacement invariant must distinguish the certified return from its start and must be checked against that witness.

records.actual_established: Every cited rank-one strict-subrank quotient overshoots the target rung by more than 1/480, and positive finite sums retain that separation.
records.failure_boundary: The obstruction is for the named strict-subrank family and its positive finite sums; it does not reject linear forms outside those assumptions.
records.prerequisites_and_assumptions: The bounds require e at least one, prefix length at least four, and positive weights for the finite-sum extension.
records.next_obligation: A prospective linear-form route must leave this strict-subrank family or change one of its explicit assumptions before it can be evaluated.

records.actual_established: Cylinder membership is exactly even integrality at its basepoint, independent of depth, and the named cofinal escape hypothesis is equivalent to the non-eventual-integrality conclusion it was intended to produce.
records.failure_boundary: The adaptive cylinder is circular as a producer; this does not settle the prime dyadic-series problem or invalidate separately formulated fixed-lattice statements.
records.prerequisites_and_assumptions: The equivalence uses the dyadic tail recurrence and the stated even-difference condition on the digit stream.
records.next_obligation: A new producer must avoid a target generated by the same orbit; the cited module identifies a fixed-lattice formulation but supplies no new arithmetic input for it.

records.route: Terminal scaled-vanishing half counterexample and finite 1/21 target
records.actual_established: A terminal scaled-vanishing sequence would yield an infinite rational half-valued counterexample, while a finite Boolean support on ranks at least two cannot sum to 1/21.
records.failure_boundary: No terminal scaled-vanishing sequence is constructed here, and neither the conditional half statement nor the finite 1/21 exclusion settles Erdős #257.
records.prerequisites_and_assumptions: The half route is conditional on a HalfTerminalOnlyScaledVanishingSequence; the 1/21 result assumes finite Boolean support with every rank at least two.
records.next_obligation: Resolve the terminal scaled-vanishing condition or supply a separately checked bridge from the finite boundary to an infinite-support question.

records.actual_established: A positive bounded integral state cannot represent a congruence class whose least positive residue is above that bound.
records.failure_boundary: This is a final finite contradiction only: the cited module does not derive its bounded integral state from rationality or construct arbitrarily late escaping windows.
records.prerequisites_and_assumptions: The finite contradiction assumes a positive modulus, a positive bounded state, the stated congruence, and a residue above the bound.
records.next_obligation: Supply both upstream inputs named by the module: the rationality-to-state reduction and late windows with the required residue escape.

records.route: Always choose the smallest angular-gap Form-A selector
records.actual_established: The cited five-point configuration has a uniquely shortest selected chord, yet the common-radius selector is blocked at radius zero and at every positive radius up to one.
records.failure_boundary: This refutes only the unconditional smallest-angular-gap rule; it does not refute the unrestricted Form-A-cut objective or settle Erdős #1041.
records.prerequisites_and_assumptions: The counterexample concerns the exact Gaussian-rational cyclic configuration and its common-radius selector defined in the cited module.
records.next_obligation: Any Form-A selector proposal must state why it avoids this unconditional smallest-gap rule and provide evidence for its own scope.

records.actual_established: Within the explicit rectangular exponent model, the two-function threshold never exceeds the classical one-function margin, with equality only at the stated endpoint.
records.failure_boundary: The comparison constructs no approximating polynomials or remainders, does not cover every rational-base method, and does not decide the Lambert value at 3/2.
records.prerequisites_and_assumptions: The model assumes rho is nonnegative and sigma is at least 1 plus rho.
records.next_obligation: A rational-base approach must first provide evidence outside this explicit rectangular model before treating it as a possible improvement.
